sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **Assignment Statements and Assignment Expressions**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Assigning values to variables
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **Assignment Statements and Assignment Expressions** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: An assignment statement stores a value in a variable using the = operator
The right side of = is evaluated first, then the result is stored in the left variable
An assignment expression has a value equal to what was assigned
The same variable can appear on both sides: x = x + 1 increments x
Variables must be declared before they can be assigned a value

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Assignment Statements and Assignment Expressions - Assigning values to variables. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: What is the value of x after: int x = 5; x = x + 3;?
questions.explanation: First x is assigned 5. Then x = x + 3 evaluates the right side (5 + 3 = 8) and assigns the result back to x, so x becomes 8.

questions.question: In the assignment statement 'y = x + 1;', which side is evaluated first?
questions.explanation: In an assignment statement, the right-hand side expression is evaluated first, then the result is assigned to the variable on the left-hand side.
